title: Social Intelligence and Critical Thinking among Faculty: A Multivariate and Network Perspective
text_snippet: Social Intelligence and Critical Thinking among Faculty: A Multivariate and Network Perspective This study examines the dynamic interplay between social intelligence and critical thinking among faculty members at Jordanian universities, framed within an educational psychology perspective. Employing a descriptivecorrelational design, data were gathered from 357 faculty members using rigorously validated measures of social intelligence (comprising Social Information Processing, Social Skills, and Social Awareness) and critical thinking (encompassing Analysis, Interpretation, Evaluation, Inference, and Self-Regulation). Results revealed robust positive correlations among most subscales, with gender differences favoring female faculty and significant variation across academic ranks, as confirmed by independent samples t-tests and multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA). Partial correlation analyses and network modeling were applied to elucidate underlying structural relationships further. The network approach identified Interpretation, Social Skills, and Self-Regulation as pivotal nodes, underscoring their critical role in integrating social and cognitive faculties. title: Coping Strategies among Female Employees of Inclusive Resource Centres (IRC) under Adverse Conditions of Professional Activity
text_snippet: Coping Strategies among Female Employees of Inclusive Resource Centres (IRC) under Adverse Conditions of Professional Activity The study aims to identify dominant coping strategies among IRC female employees under adverse conditions of professional activity. “Emotional exhaustion”, “depersonalisation”, “anxiety”, “level of resilience”, and “depression” were found to be most dependent on coping strategies. “Reduced personal accomplishment” was found to be the most autonomous occupational burnout parameter. Comparison of coping strategies across grouping variables revealed that both non-productive and productive coping strategies prevail when “emotional exhaustion”, “depersonalisation”, “anxiety”, and “depression” are pronounced. The study suggests that adverse conditions of professional activity trigger defence mechanisms, mobilising available resources through the compensatory function of self-preservation and the maintenance of mental integrity

title: The Nature of Relationships between Temperamental Traits, Planning Ability and Inhibitory control
text_snippet: The Nature of Relationships between Temperamental Traits, Planning Ability and Inhibitory control The article raises the important issue of the relationship between temperamental traits (negative affect, surgency, effortful control) and the ability to plan with mediated inhibitory control in 5–6-year-old children. The study included 101 children (44.6% girls). The following instruments were used: the Children’s Behavior Questionnaire (Rothbart et al., 2001; in Polish adaptation by Lipska et al., 2022), the Children’s Card Sorting Test (Jabłoński et al., 2018), and the Tower of London (Culbertson & Zillmer, 2011). Although the results did not support the hypothesis of the role of inhibitory control as a mediator, they did reveal the key role of effortful control in shaping planning processes. The relationship between effortful control and planning may be direct, arising more from effortful control’s earlier developmental timing than inhibition processes. These results have practical significance and provide guidance for psychologists, teachers, educators, and parents.

title: Courtesy Stigma in Light of the Biographical Experiences of the Mothers of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
text_snippet: Courtesy Stigma in Light of the Biographical Experiences of the Mothers of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) The paper analyzes courtesy stigma in mothers raising children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) through individual life histories. Using a narrative method and interviews, the study reconstructs and interprets their experiences, revealing mechanisms and consequences of stigma. Data were analyzed via a three-component model of affiliate stigma: affective, cognitive, and behavioral. Findings show emotions of fear, anger, guilt, shame, low self-esteem, and self-stigma. Behaviorally, both withdrawal and active struggle for the child’s welfare emerged. Conclusions highlight the need for systemic psychological support, institutional integration, partnership with parents, and inclusion of their perspectives in educational, therapeutic, and social solutions.

title: Case Study of a Student with Edwards Syndrome
text_snippet: Case Study of a Student with Edwards Syndrome This paper addresses the issue of the educational process for a student with a severe genetic disorder with an unfavourable prognosis, known as Edwards syndrome. It presents the results of a qualitative research study in the form of a case study of a student with Edwards syndrome. The aim of the paper is to characterize the educational specifics of a student with Edwards syndrome and the forms and methods used in their education. The research findings indicate that although the student’s developmental potential is limited, with the provision of an appropriate environment, support, and professional care, the student is able to make individual progress, particularly in the areas of communication, socialization, and basic self-care.

title: An Inquiry-Based E-Module Using Black Soldier Fly Maggots to Enhance Students’ Science Process Skills through Deep Learning
text_snippet: An Inquiry-Based E-Module Using Black Soldier Fly Maggots to Enhance Students’ Science Process Skills through Deep Learning Science process skills are essential in biology education; however, students often have limited opportunities to engage in inquiry-oriented learning that promotes deep understanding. This quantitative study examined the effectiveness of an inquiry-based e-module using Black Soldier Fly maggots to enhance students’ science process skills through deep learning. The study implemented a quasi-experimental design with tenth-grade students from a public high school. The results show that students using the inquiry-based e-module achieved significantly higher science process skills than those receiving conventional instruction, even after controlling for prior knowledge. These findings demonstrate the pedagogical value of inquiry-oriented digital learning resources in strengthening scientific competencies in biology education.

title: The Effect of the Program “Ideal” on University Students’ Critical Thinking Dispositions And Skills
text_snippet: The Effect of the Program “Ideal” on University Students’ Critical Thinking Dispositions And Skills The aim of the study was to design and pilot-implement a mixed critical thinking development program within a specific course of a university study program, and to examine its effect on students’ critical thinking skills and dispositions. A quasi-experimental design was employed, comparing scores obtained through the Critical Thinking Skills Test (CTST; Eğmir & Ocak, 2016) and the Critical Thinking Disposition Scale (CTDS; Sosu, 2013) between an experimental group (n = 32) and a control group (n = 22). The results demonstrated a statistically significant increase in the levels of critical thinking skills and dispositions in the experimental group. The effect of the program persisted over time. The study provides empirical evidence supporting the implementation of intervention programs aimed at developing critical thinking within higher education.

title: Empirical Validation of the Teuku Umar Leadership Scale: A PLS-SEM Approach Grounded in Local and Islamic Values
text_snippet: Empirical Validation of the Teuku Umar Leadership Scale: A PLS-SEM Approach Grounded in Local and Islamic Values This study validates the Teuku Umar Leadership (TUL) scale, a leadership instrument grounded in local and Islamic values within the Indonesian context. Data were collected from 551 teachers in West Aceh District using multistage random sampling and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.1.0.9. The results confirm that 40 of 49 indicators across eight dimensions are valid and reliable, with brave, virtuous, and intelligent traits contributing most strongly to the construct. The findings support the empirical robustness of the TUL model and offer a culturally grounded framework for leadership development and educational practice.

title: From Passion to Psychological Well-Being in Teachers: Pathways Through Resilience
text_snippet: From Passion to Psychological Well-Being in Teachers: Pathways Through Resilience This quantitative study examined how harmonious and obsessive forms of non work and teacher passion relate to teachers’ psychological well being, considering the mediating role of resilience. The sample comprised 543 teachers who completed validated measures of passion, resilience and psychological well being. Path analysis showed that harmonious passion in both domains (teacher and non-work) was positively associated with well being through higher resilience, whereas obsessive passion was unrelated to well being. The model including both types of harmonious passion simultaneously provided the most accurate explanation. The findings highlight the adaptive value of harmonious passion and the central role of resilience in supporting teachers’ well being.

title: Integrating Ethnocultural Content into Future Teachers’ Project Design Activities: Development and Quasi-Experimental Validation of an Educational Model
text_snippet: Integrating Ethnocultural Content into Future Teachers’ Project Design Activities: Development and Quasi-Experimental Validation of an Educational Model This study developed and quasi-experimentally validated the Ethnocultural Project Design Integration Model (EPDIM) for future teachers. Using pre/post questionnaires, context-specific divergent-thinking tasks, expert project assessment, and motif analysis, the study compared an experimental and a control group. The experimental group showed greater gains in ethnocultural awareness, emotional-value attitude, practical readiness, creativity, and project quality, supporting both hypotheses. Final projects most often used vegetal (42.9%) and geometric motifs (31.4%), followed by zoomorphic (14.3%) and mythical motifs (11.4%). EPDIM integrates cultural-semantic and critical-ethical analysis, craft interaction, digital project work, and reflective expert assessment. Its transferability beyond the Ukrainian context requires further validation.

title: Cultural Intelligence as a Mediator Between Language Learning Strategies and Intercultural Communicative Competence
text_snippet: Cultural Intelligence as a Mediator Between Language Learning Strategies and Intercultural Communicative Competence This research investigated whether cultural intelligence (CQ) mediates the relationship between language learning strategies (LLS) and intercultural communicative competence (ICC). It employed a non-experimental correlational design and a mediation analysis to ascertain the relationships among variables. Using a stratified random sampling procedure, 258 pre-service teachers participated in this research. Adapted questionnaires were administered to the respondents. The hypothesized mediation model was assessed using standard algorithm bootstrapping in SmartPLS 4.0. Findings revealed that the pre-service teachers demonstrated high levels of LLS use, particularly the metacognitive strategy. Results also show high CQ and ICC. Among the domains, the respondents demonstrated the highest levels of metacognitive CQ and ICC attitudes. Finally, the mediation analysis suggests that CQ mediates the relationship between LLS and ICC, suggesting that language learning activities should facilitate improvements in cultural knowledge, behavior, and motivation among pre-service teachers.

title: The Impact of The Learning Process, Teacher Quality, and School Management on The Academic Achievement of Elementary School Students In Indonesia
text_snippet: The Impact of The Learning Process, Teacher Quality, and School Management on The Academic Achievement of Elementary School Students In Indonesia Primary education is an essential cornerstone in the progress of a nation. Elementary school-age children serve as the primary entry point for engaging with the social environment, which has the potential to influence character development. This study examines the impact of the learning process, teacher competence, and school administration on the academic performance of primary school students in the Special Region of Yogyakarta Province. Data were collected from 561 schools using census sampling procedures, employing an explanatory quantitative approach and a cross-sectional design. The analysis results indicate that the learning process alone—when considered independently from teacher competence and school administration—does not significantly affect the quality of graduates. In contrast, the calibre of educators and the effectiveness of school administration have a profound positive impact on graduate outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of allocating resources toward improving teacher competence and school management to enhance the standards of primary education in the Special Region of Yogyakarta. title: Students’ Characteristics and Learning Environment: Predictors to PATH FIT Engagement
text_snippet: Students’ Characteristics and Learning Environment: Predictors to PATH FIT Engagement This quantitative descriptive-correlational study examined how students’ characteristics and learning environment predict engagement in Physical Activity Towards Health and Fitness (PATH FIT) subjects. A researchermade questionnaire validated by three experts and pilot-tested on 30 students (Cronbach’s α = 0.89) was administered to 299 randomly selected first-year students at Camiguin Polytechnic State College during the second semester of 2022–2023. Results showed high levels of student characteristics (M = 4.17), learning environment (M = 4.27), and PATH FIT engagement (M = 4.30). title: Ego-Resilience and Subjective Happiness among Upper Elementary School Students: The Mediating Roles of Cognitive and Affective Empathy
text_snippet: Ego-Resilience and Subjective Happiness among Upper Elementary School Students: The Mediating Roles of Cognitive and Affective Empathy This study investigated how ego-resilience influences the subjective happiness of 643 upper elementary school students, specifically focusing on the mediating roles of cognitive and affective empathy. Mediation analysis revealed significant positive correlations among all variables. Both cognitive and affective empathy partially mediated the relationship between ego-resilience and happiness, with cognitive empathy exerting a notably stronger effect. This underscores the importance of metacognitive perspective-taking development in late childhood. The findings suggest that enhancing egoresilience and fostering empathy through social-emotional learning are vital strategies for promoting children’s subjective well-being in educational environments.

title: Personal Resources for Buffering Against Distress in Students
text_snippet: Personal Resources for Buffering Against Distress in Students The research aims to identify students’ personal characteristics and abilities that possess resource potential to buffer against distress. Overall poise, self-efficacy, involvement, control, and risk-taking were found to be personal characteristics and integral abilities possessing resource potential. It was established that obvious manifestations of neuroticism, depressiveness, irritability, emotional lability, and self-doubt are personal correlates of stressogenic maladaptation and distress in students. The findings suggest that heightened motivation for success in stressful situations is a quasi-compensatory mechanism of psychological defence and situational conditional maintenance of psychological integrity. Further research will examine the factors mitigating negative effects of academic and psychological stress.

title: Internet Addiction Markers of Mental Health Disorders Among University Youth
text_snippet: Internet Addiction Markers of Mental Health Disorders Among University Youth The study aims to determine the internet addiction markers of mental health disorders among university youth. Statistically significant differences were identified among the three groups based on the severity of internet addiction – low, medium, and high. Differences were found in all studied parameters based on the grouping variables “internet addiction” and “problematic use of mobile phone”. It was summarized that external markers of mental health showed direct correlations, while internal markers showed inverse correlations with internet addiction at a high level of significance.

title: Understanding Social Entrepreneurial Self-Efficacy: The Contributions of Entrepreneurship Education, Empathy, and Social Responsibility
text_snippet: Understanding Social Entrepreneurial Self-Efficacy: The Contributions of Entrepreneurship Education, Empathy, and Social Responsibility Social entrepreneurship has become increasingly important in addressing complex social problems through innovative and sustainable approaches. This study examined whether entrepreneurship education and empathy enhance social entrepreneurial self-efficacy through the mediating role of social responsibility among university students. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 816 final-year students at private universities in Indonesia. Adapted and validated scales were administered, and the data were analysed using mediation analysis. The findings revealed that entrepreneurship education and empathy significantly influenced social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, both directly and indirectly through social responsibility. Social responsibility partially mediated these relationships, indicating the importance of value internalization in entrepreneurial learning processes. The results highlight the importance of integrating social-emotional learning and social values into entrepreneurship education to foster students’ confidence in creating social impact.

title: Development of an Interactive Digital Book Model for Anti-Corruption Education in Higher Education
text_snippet: Development of an Interactive Digital Book Model for Anti-Corruption Education in Higher Education This research emphasizes the importance of instilling anti-corruption values such as honesty, discipline, responsibility, and fairness through an interactive digital book designed for anti-corruption and social studies education. Using a Research and Development method, the study involved students from Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia and applied interviews, observations, FGDs, and questionnaires. The book, developed in three stages using Canva, integrates cognitive, affective, and psychomotor domains. Validation results indicated satisfactory quality, and limited trials showed strong student understanding and value internalization. The findings conclude that the interactive digital book effectively fosters students’ anti-corruption character, supporting its use in hybrid learning environments.

title: Effects of AI-Generated Model Essays on Argumentative EFL Writing: A Quasi-Experimental Study
text_snippet: Effects of AI-Generated Model Essays on Argumentative EFL Writing: A Quasi-Experimental Study This quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study tested whether guided engagement with AI-generated argumentative model essays plus explicit editing instruction produced larger gains in EFL argumentative writing than teacher handout exemplars. Ninety-six third-year undergraduates (two intact groups, n = 48 each) completed timed argumentative tasks before and after six weekly 90-minute sessions. Two assistant-lecturer raters scored essays blind to condition using an analytic rubric; objective indices (type– token ratio; errors/100 words) complemented ratings. Paired t tests showed within-group gains; an independent-samples t test on gain scores favored the experimental group (d = 0.72), with largest effects in lexical range and organization. Two experimental focus groups elucidated editing-to-transfer mechanisms.

title: University Students’ Perceptions and the Use of ChatGPT for Writing in English
text_snippet: University Students’ Perceptions and the Use of ChatGPT for Writing in English This study explored university students’ perceptions of and actual use of ChatGPT as a writing tool in English, and examined how gender, year of study, field of study, and English proficiency influence their attitudes toward technology. A quantitative research design was employed, surveying 197 English-writing students at the University of Prishtina via an online questionnaire. Structural equation modeling (SEM) assessed the relationships among demographic variables, perceived efficacy, benefits, drawbacks, motivation, and overall attitude toward ChatGPT. Students’ attitudes are predominantly driven by their perception of ChatGPT’s efficacy in improving their writing skills. Perceived benefits, such as enhanced writing quality and increased motivation, positively influence motivation and overall attitude. Demographic factors exerted only modest effects: gender and year of study influenced how benefits and drawbacks were viewed, while field of study and English proficiency had smaller effects.

title: Does Multicultural Personality Foster Resilience and Forgiveness in Emerging Adults: Evidence from Students in Mumbai
text_snippet: Does Multicultural Personality Foster Resilience and Forgiveness in Emerging Adults: Evidence from Students in Mumbai Introduction: Mumbai city attracts students from various backgrounds, cultures, religions, languages, and castes. Even though the city is considered a multicultural mosaic, it is fractured on the basis of class, caste, and religion. Multiple studies have shown that in a multicultural society, there are cultural differences which can also present challenges such as misunderstanding, conflicts & communication barriers among people. The present study has been planned to fill the gap in the literature by assessing the role of multicultural personality on resilience and forgiveness, and to examine the predictors and correlates. Methodology: A correlational study among 468 Indian students studying undergraduate and postgraduate courses was assessed using well-reliable and valid psychological scales to measure multicultural personality, forgiveness, and resilience, and various demographic variables like age, religion, caste, gender, and socioeconomic status. Results: It was seen that a multicultural personality was significantly correlated (moderate) with forgiveness and resilience. It has emerged that multicultural personality traits were a significant predictor of forgiveness and resili

title: Assessing Social Sciences Students’ Attitudes Toward Statistics: Validation Study of the Polish Version of SATS-36
text_snippet: Assessing Social Sciences Students’ Attitudes Toward Statistics: Validation Study of the Polish Version of SATS-36 This study validated the Polish SATS-36 (Survey of Attitudes toward Statistics, Schau, 2003) among 423 social sciences students from randomly selected universities using item-level confirmatory factor analysis. The six-factor structure aligned with the original but required modifications, including removing four items from the Difficulty subscale. Five subscales showed high reliability and stability. Criterion validity was confirmed through correlations with math achievement, self-rated math ability, and prior statistics experience. The Polish SATS-36 is the first validated tool for assessing attitudes toward statistics in Poland, enabling cross-cultural comparisons and supporting research to improve learning outcomes.

title: Pedagogical Determinants of the Development of Teachers’ General Competencies in Professional Preparation
text_snippet: Pedagogical Determinants of the Development of Teachers’ General Competencies in Professional Preparation The article presents a model for measuring the components of educational intervention aimed at the development of general competencies among students enrolled in teacher education programmes. It is argued that traditional approaches to pedagogical experimentation do not allow researchers to determine the specific contribution of individual components of educational intervention to competency-based learning outcomes. The proposed model provides for the identification of partial pedagogical factors and their quantitative assessment using two experimental approaches: accumulation and separation. The model enables the comparison of outcomes under conditions of both combined and isolated effects of pedagogical factors. The experimental validation demonstrated that individual components of educational intervention differ in both the strength and nature of their impact on the development of general competencies, while the structuring of factors modifies the configuration of final learning outcomes. The findings suggest that the proposed model is an effective tool for improving the precision of pedagogical research and can be employed to enhance competency-based educational programmes in t

title: Divine Dichotomies: Gender Differences in the Impact of Spirituality on Positive Student Outcomes
text_snippet: Divine Dichotomies: Gender Differences in the Impact of Spirituality on Positive Student Outcomes This study uses Self-Determination Theory and Social Role Theory to empirically examine the relationships between spirituality and four key developmental outcomes—self-confidence, flexibility, volunteering, and helpseeking behaviors—among first-year undergraduate students, with a focus on gender differences. Survey data from 326 first-year undergraduates in the western U. S. indicate that higher levels of self-reported spirituality are positively associated with self-confidence, flexibility, volunteering, and help-seeking behaviors. The positive relationship between spirituality and self-confidence, flexibility, and volunteering was more pronounced in men, whereas the association between spirituality and help-seeking behaviors was stronger in women. These results show the importance of considering gender when exploring the impact of spirituality on student development and suggest that integrating spiritual support into educational programs may foster holistic growth among undergraduates.

title: The Study of the Value Intelligence Influence on Student’s AI Use in Education and Scientific Work
text_snippet: The Study of the Value Intelligence Influence on Student’s AI Use in Education and Scientific Work This investigation aims to answer the question: is there a connection between the level of “Value Intelligence” and the perception of “Artificial Intelligence” among students and whether students with different attitudes towards artificial intelligence using have differences in positive and negative values assimilation. The study involved 361 students from four leading universities in Ukraine. The study involved determining the level of value intelligence using the author’s scale and identifying the perception of artificial intelligence and its ethical use by the authors’ developed questionnaire. The results indicate the presence of a reliable direct correlation between the level of value intelligence and artificial intelligence using. The predictive role of value intelligence in determining the level of perception of artificial intelligence was revealed. Clustering showed the presence of three models of artificial intelligence perception among modern students and differences in the positive and negative values expression and assimilation in these three clusters were established. Implications for practice, policy, and future research on the use of AI and value intelligence are disc

title: Future Time Perspective and Its Relationship with Health Behaviours and Well-Being Among School Adolescents in Poland
text_snippet: Future Time Perspective and Its Relationship with Health Behaviours and Well-Being Among School Adolescents in Poland Adolescents’ future time perspective (FTP) is linked to academic and mental health outcomes, yet its determinants remain insufficiently understood. This study examined associations between FTP and sociodemographic, psychological, and behavioural factors in 9,200 Polish students aged 12– 19 (54.7% girls) surveyed online in 2024. FTP was assessed using the five item scale; predictors included KIDSCREEN-27 dimensions, school stress, depression risk (WHO-5), physical activity, and risky behaviours. Linear regression identified the school environment (β = 0.256) as the strongest positive predictor, followed by physical well-being, age, physical activity, and parent–child relations, while depression risk and city residence were negative predictors. The model explained 19.5% of variance, with stronger effects among girls.

title: Facilitation-Based Approaches as a Means of Cultivating Media Literacy in Educators and Administrators of Educational Institutions
text_snippet: Facilitation-Based Approaches as a Means of Cultivating Media Literacy in Educators and Administrators of Educational Institutions The purpose of this study was to investigate and evaluate the importance of facilitation in cultivating media literacy among teachers and heads of educational institutions. Sample comprised 315 teachers aged 22 to 59 years. Methods: The study employed the MLPS, the Media Literacy questionnaire, and the Critical Thinking test developed by L. Starkey. Statistical analyses were conducted using both Student’s t-test and the Kruskal–Wallis test. The results showed that teachers have average levels of critical thinking and media literacy; male teachers have more developed critical thinking skills, whilst female teachers have higher levels of media literacy (p ≤ 0.01). Media literacy was highest in the 35–46 age group (p ≤ 0.01). The control group showed an increase in critical thinking and media literacy scores in the experimental group compared to the control group (p≤0.01).

title: Workplace-Based Vocational Training as Complementary to Formal TVET Provisions
text_snippet: Workplace-Based Vocational Training as Complementary to Formal TVET Provisions This study aimed to explore the nature of workplace-based vocational training (WBT) practice and its potential as a provision of vocational training in Eritrea, with a focus on public organizations. A total of 230 employers were selected via availability sampling, while 12 were chosen through purposive sampling techniques. The research adopted a survey dominated mixed-methods approach, utilizing both self-administered questionnaires and semi-structured interviews for data collection. Descriptive, inferential, and thematic analyses were employed to interpret the findings. WBT was identified as a cost-effective alternative to traditional TVET despite organizational hesitancy due to limited readiness. These findings enhance our understanding of the relationship between organizational preparedness, WBT benefits, and its actual implementation. The implications suggest that while formal vocational training may be costly for youth access, public sectors can play a crucial role in implementing WBT. Based on these results, it is recommended to prioritize WBT as an intervention to address unemployment and social exclusion among disadvantaged youth groups.

title: New Categorization of Areas of Interest When Reading Physics Textbooks for Primary Schools Using Eye Tracking
text_snippet: New Categorization of Areas of Interest When Reading Physics Textbooks for Primary Schools Using Eye Tracking The present study aims to propose and verify a new categorization of areas of interest (AOI) when reading physics textbooks for primary schools and to compare attention patterns across three types of textbooks (classical, hybrid, interactive). The primary research method is eye tracking, which is supplemented by short semi-structured interviews. The research group consisted of 24 primary school students. Four categories of AOI students were identified: Brief Review, Shallow Review, In-Depth Processing, Intense Focus. The study provides textbook authors with universally applicable guidance on how to revise their works quickly, easily and at an acceptable financial cost, and then improve them to better meet the needs of their users after discovering strengths and weaknesses. The study outlines possible solutions to increase the attention of textbook users.

title: The Impact of the Engoo Platform on Students’ Oral Reading Skills and Perceptions of Elementary School Level
text_snippet: The Impact of the Engoo Platform on Students’ Oral Reading Skills and Perceptions of Elementary School Level Recent reports highlight a persistent literacy crisis among elementary school students in Indonesia, particularly in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) contexts. Despite the growing use of digital learning tools, empirical evidence on the effectiveness of online tutoring platforms such as Engoo at the elementary level remains limited. This study employed a pre-experimental pre-test and post-test design involving 150 fifth-grade students from 10 elementary schools in Purworejo Regency, Central Java, to examine the effectiveness of Engoo and students’ perceptions of its use. Data were collected through an oral reading test assessing pronunciation, accuracy, fluency, and comprehension, as well as a 15-item Likert-scale questionnaire. title: The Sense of Realism in Sustainable Nonformal Adult Learning in the Digital Space
text_snippet: The Sense of Realism in Sustainable Nonformal Adult Learning in the Digital Space Sustainable development is a central challenge encompassing social, economic, and environmental dimensions. Within adult education, sustainable nonformal learning plays a particularly important role, and the Wikinomic space offers an innovative platform to support this process. Assuming that respondents’ assessments of the value of online learning are influenced by a relatively small set of determinants, we employed a Bayesian framework to identify them. Our results indicate that five key variables most reliably shape adults’ evaluations of online learning, tending to produce pragmatic, moderate appraisals rather than maximally enthusiastic ones.

title: Bully-Victims as a Distinct Psychosocial Category: Readiness for Aggression and Prosocial Tendencies
text_snippet: Bully-Victims as a Distinct Psychosocial Category: Readiness for Aggression and Prosocial Tendencies This article examines the bully–victim profile in terms of readiness for interpersonal aggression and prosocial tendencies. A quantitative study was conducted among 566 students in Grades 6–8, with comparative analyses based on a high-involvement subsample. Results show that bully–victims display the highest levels across all aggression-readiness mechanisms, while no significant between-group differences appear in declared prosociality. However, a discrepancy between prosocial declarations and normative valuation indicates regulatory inconsistency and internal complexity. The findings support a regulatory-profile approach to identifying bully–victims and designing more precisely targeted school-based interventions.

title: Teacher-Student Interaction in Vietnamese Primary Schools: An Analysis from Macro Level to Micro Level
text_snippet: Teacher-Student Interaction in Vietnamese Primary Schools: An Analysis from Macro Level to Micro Level This study examines teacher-student interactions in Vietnam’s educational reform, comparing public and private schools and identifying influencing factors. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research involved surveys (126 teachers, 189 students), interviews (5 teachers, 4 students), and classroom observations (4 classes). Results showed that interactions were mostly cooperative, emphasizing understanding and helpfulness. However, students rated strictness higher and freedom lower than teachers, highlighting differing expectations. Public schools showed more structure, while private schools emphasized flexibility and support. Influencing factors included social media, school type, parental involvement, and student behavior. Social media increased teachers’ emotional demands, while parental socioeconomic status shaped authority and engagement. Student misbehavior posed challenges for maintaining discipline.

title: International internships as the instrument for enhancement of academic mobility of students of higher educational institutions
text_snippet: International internships as the instrument for enhancement of academic mobility of students of higher educational institutions This study aims to detect the influence of international internships on the academic mobility of students of higher educational institutions, as well as their professional development and intercultural integration. Survey method, Intercultural Competence Scale, Career Readiness Competencies (NACE), engagement of focus groups, as well as statistical methods such as t-test, χ²-test and correlation analysis were used in the study. The results showed that international internships significantly influence the development of the core competencies. In particular, the average score for communicative skills increased from 3.9 to 4.6 after participation in the internship, for critical thinking — from 3.8 to 4.5, and for teamwork — from 3.7 to 4.4.

title: Young Ages, Big Decisions: Development and Initial Validation of the Multidimensional Financial Literacy Scale for Adolescents
text_snippet: Young Ages, Big Decisions: Development and Initial Validation of the Multidimensional Financial Literacy Scale for Adolescents This study developed the Financial Literacy Scale for Adolescents (FLSADO) to assess adolescents’ financial literacy and examined its psychometric properties. Exploratory (n = 382) and confirmatory (n = 512) factor analyses revealed an 18-item scale with three subscales: conscious consumption, savings and future planning, and the meaning of money, explaining 50.16% of the variance. A brief five-item version (FLSADO-5) was created based on EFA loadings, representing all sub-dimensions and accounting for 33.92% of the variance. CFA supported both the three-factor structure of FLSADO and the unidimensional structure of FLSADO-5. Internal consistency coefficients indicated good reliability for both versions. Correlations with external measures supported concurrent validity.

title: Children’s Interest in Outdoor Play and Its use in the Educational Environment
text_snippet: Children’s Interest in Outdoor Play and Its use in the Educational Environment Outdoor play represents a natural part of children’s lives both at home and in school settings. This article presents the results of an empirical study focused on the use of outdoor play in the educational process. The research applied both quantitative and qualitative approaches and was conducted in 2023–2024. A total of 206 respondents from Slovakia participated: 130 children aged 5 to 10 years, 72 preschool and primary school teachers, and 4 school psychologists. The aim was to identify children’s interest in outdoor play, to analyze teachers’ views on its implementation in pre-primary and primary education, and to interpret school psychologists’ perspectives on its significance. The findings confirmed that children show interest in various forms of outdoor play and that teachers make use of it in the educational process, with the extent of use depending mainly on teaching experience.

title: The Effects of Technology-Enhanced Deep Learning on Autonomy of EFL Learners with Disabilities
text_snippet: The Effects of Technology-Enhanced Deep Learning on Autonomy of EFL Learners with Disabilities Many studies have examined the impact of technology-enhanced deep learning on learner autonomy, but few have focused on EFL classes for learners with disabilities. This study aims to describe the effects of a technology-enhanced deep learning strategy on the autonomy of learners with disabilities in EFL settings. A quasi-experimental design was used, involving sixty-two EFL learners with disabilities in Indonesia. Data were collected through close-ended questionnaires and semi-structured interviews about learner autonomy in English classes. The findings showed that there was a significant effect of technology-enhanced deep learning on learner autonomy. Factors influencing autonomy included psychological aspects, learning strategies, cognitive and metacognitive abilities, critical thinking, teacher roles, tasks, and learning environment. Activities such as challenging tasks, flexible task completion, peer collaboration, and diverse learning resources helped foster learner autonomy. The study concludes that technology-enhanced deep learning can serve as an effective alternative to promote learner autonomy in English language classes.

title: Challenges of Collaborative Learning of Code Refactoring in a Ukrainian University
text_snippet: Challenges of Collaborative Learning of Code Refactoring in a Ukrainian University This study investigates Ukrainian software engineering students’ perceptions of collaborative code refactoring in a “Software Construction” course. Using two Likert scales and multiple-choice questions, 248 students evaluated general course satisfaction and collaborative learning experiences. Results showed lower satisfaction with collaborative tasks compared to general course satisfaction. Students recognized professional relevance and skill development benefits, but faced significant challenges, including reluctance to engage with others’ code and insufficient preparation for the collaborative code refactoring. Correlation analysis revealed strong motivation-growth relationships in collaborative contexts. Findings suggest that addressing technical preparation, cultural adaptation, and process clarity is essential for successful collaborative implementation.

title: Quantitative Estimation of Knowledge Level in Fundamental Medical Academic Subjects Among Students as a Manifestation of Educational Losses in Ukraine During a Full-scale Russian Invasion
text_snippet: Quantitative Estimation of Knowledge Level in Fundamental Medical Academic Subjects Among Students as a Manifestation of Educational Losses in Ukraine During a Full-scale Russian Invasion The Ukrainian education system has faced unprecedentedly difficult circumstances for the past 4 years due to the consequences of the military aggression of the Russian Federation. Medical education has faced significant restrictions and obstacles to normal functioning, including a decrease in the number of students, a reduction in financial resources, the destruction of the material and technical base, the loss of human resources, and disruptions to access to education. The results of medical students in passing the qualificative exam indicate a decrease in quantitative and qualitative indicators since 2022, which can be regarded as a manifestation of educational losses in the country.

title: Trauma Experience in Music School Graduates: In-Depth Interviews Analysis
text_snippet: Trauma Experience in Music School Graduates: In-Depth Interviews Analysis The present study investigates the adverse experiences of students in music schools. It examines their potential effects on adult functioning, along with indicating the similarities between the reported symptoms and those characteristic of complex Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (cPTSD). This qualitative inquiry involves six music school graduates who participated in in-depth interviews focusing on their educational experiences and relationships with teachers and mentors. The findings reveal the existence of potentially traumatic experiences, including instances of physical and psychological violence, in the course of education. Concurrently, it is essential to acknowledge that this area warrants further investigation employing strong research methodologies.

title: Causative Agents of Science Learning among Elementary Students
text_snippet: Causative Agents of Science Learning among Elementary Students The study analyzed the causative agents as determinants that enhance or hinder the learning process from lessening difficulties in science instruction. Therefore, overall student academic achievement must be diagnosed. Several determinants were extracted from reports affecting learning in science; this study points out the intrinsic and extrinsic determinants that affect science learning among elementary students. Determinants were identified using descriptive-correlational research employing Cohen’s Kappa Index (CKI) = 0.70 among 250 student respondents. Analysis showed that four determinants are causative agents that significantly affected their learning in science: previous grades in science, parents’ education, combined monthly income, and availability of books. A supportive academic-laden environment orientation and other motivational influences can help unprepared and less knowledgeable students understand the complex nature of science subjects.
